title: Website review report
scopeLine: {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} · {devices} · {runs} runs
summaryScope: We reviewed {pages, plural, one {# public page} other {# public pages}} of {site} on {devices}, {runs} times each with a fresh browser.
summaryNone: We found no confirmed problems: nothing failed in every run.
summaryFound: We found {count, plural, one {# confirmed problem} other {# confirmed problems}}: {count, plural, one {it shows} other {they show}} in every run, not by chance.

area.frontend: Frontend: what visitors see and use
area.backend: Backend: the server, seen from outside

areaHint.frontend: Design, accessibility, behaviour, performance, mobile and content.

severityLegend: Severity: critical (stops people from using something or exposes it), serious (affects many people), moderate (annoying or harmful), minor (worth fixing).

where.everyPage: on every page reviewed: most likely a shared template

steps.open: Open {page} on {devices}, in a private window (no cookies, no cache).
steps.wait: Wait until the page has finished loading.

shotCaption: Screenshot of {page}. For accessibility problems, the affected elements are outlined.
perfNote: Measured from the computer that made the review, not data from real visitors: the median of the runs, rated by Google's thresholds. Only what is poor in every run counts as a problem.
passive: It was a passive review, like an attentive visitor's: nothing on the site was changed.
passivePublic: Only public pages were visited, without signing in.
passiveNoActions: No form was sent and no button pressed: pages were only opened and addresses requested with GET or HEAD. Links that look like actions (sign out, delete, unsubscribe, add to cart…) and technical routes (/api/, /admin/…) were never requested.
passiveVerified: A problem appears here only when it was seen in all {runs} runs. Those seen only sometimes are left out.
passiveLab: Performance was measured in the lab from the computer that made the review; real visitors may get other times.
passiveSession: An access saved by the owner was used to see signed-in pages.
noProblems: There are no confirmed problems to list.

fix.generic: See the details in EXEGEZIS and fix the cause on the site.
fix.contrast: Use a text colour with a contrast of at least {required}:1 on its background.
fix.contrastColor: Change the text colour to {color} (contrast {ratio}:1; the minimum is {required}:1). It is a calculated suggestion: check it with your design.
fix.tap: Make every element at least 24×24 px, for example with {y} px of padding above and below and {x} px on the sides, or leave 24 px between the centres of two neighbours.
fix.a11y: Fix the element following the accessibility rule {rule} (WCAG). Explanation and examples: {link}
fix.js-exceptions: A JavaScript error interrupts the page. Ask whoever develops it to fix it: the exact message is in the inspection's details.
fix.console-errors: The page logs an error. Ask whoever develops it to look at its cause (the exact message is in the details).
fix.failed-requests: A file or service of the site does not answer properly. Check that it exists and that the server serves it without an error.
fix.broken-links: Fix or remove the link, or redirect (301) the old address to the new one.
fix.mixed-content: Load that resource over https:// (or from a copy on your own site).
fix.mobile-scroll: Make nothing wider than the screen: images and tables with max-width: 100% or their own scrolling.
fix.mobile-text-size: Use text of at least 12 px (16 px is better for the main text).

mobile-viewport.missing: Add to the head the meta viewport tag with content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1".
mobile-viewport.blocks-zoom: Remove user-scalable=no and maximum-scale from the meta viewport so people can zoom.

fix.mobile-fixed-overlap: Make fixed elements (bars, banners) smaller so they do not cover the content on phones, or let people close them.

perf-vitals.lcp: The main content takes long to appear: compress and resize large images, serve the content without waiting for scripts, and use faster hosting or a CDN.
perf-vitals.cls: The content moves while loading: give images, ads and embeds a width and height, and do not insert content above what is already shown.
perf-vitals.tbt: JavaScript blocks the page: remove or defer scripts not needed while loading and split long tasks.

heavy-resources.heavy-image: Compress the image and serve it as WebP or AVIF, at the size it is shown.
heavy-resources.legacy-format: Convert the image to WebP or AVIF: they usually weigh 25–50% less for the same quality.
heavy-resources.oversized-image: Serve a smaller version of the image (srcset) for the size it is shown at.
heavy-resources.uncompressed: Turn on gzip or Brotli compression on the server for JavaScript and CSS.
heavy-resources.no-cache: Add caching headers: Cache-Control: max-age=31536000, immutable for versioned files, or at least an ETag.

fix.slow-response: The server is slow to start answering: check the hosting, turn on page caching or use a CDN.

security-headers.hsts-missing: Add the header Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains.
security-headers.csp-missing: Add a Content-Security-Policy, starting with: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'self', and widen it for what the site uses.
security-headers.framing-allowed: Stop other sites from showing your pages in a frame: Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (and X-Frame-Options: SAMEORIGIN).
security-headers.permissions-missing: Add a Permissions-Policy, for example: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=().

cookies.not-secure: Mark the cookie with the Secure attribute.
cookies.not-httponly: Mark the session cookie HttpOnly so no script can read it.
cookies.no-samesite: Add SameSite=Lax to the cookie (or Strict).

https.no-https: Install an HTTPS certificate (free with Let's Encrypt, for example) and redirect all traffic to https://.
https.http-entry-no-redirect: Redirect (301) every http:// address to its https:// version and add HSTS.
https.http-no-redirect: Redirect (301) http:// to https:// across the site and add HSTS.
https.cert-invalid: Renew or fix the HTTPS certificate (chain and names): browsers warn visitors that the site is not secure.
https.cert-expiring: Renew the HTTPS certificate before it expires, or automate the renewal.
https.long-redirects: Link straight to the final address to avoid chained redirects.

site-config.robots-error: Make /robots.txt answer 200 (or 404 when there is none), never a server error.
site-config.robots-missing: Create a robots.txt with «User-agent: *», «Allow: /» and the sitemap's address.
site-config.robots-html: Serve a real text robots.txt at /robots.txt.
site-config.sitemap-missing: Create a sitemap.xml with the site's pages and name it in robots.txt.
site-config.sitemap-error: Make the sitemap answer without an error.
site-config.sitemap-invalid: Fix the sitemap: it must be XML with urlset or sitemapindex.
site-config.sitemap-url: Remove from the sitemap the pages that no longer exist.
site-config.soft-404: Make addresses that do not exist answer with a 404 (or 410) status, not 200.
